And to address ShonaNingyo's concern, Bloody Sunday probably came about as the result of an active realignment event in progress where the EoE expanded outwards in a sudden burst after being relatively compact for an unusually long time, ending up encompassing several of the more popular rides that had previously been outside it…

There is the mention of "destroying the SCP via airstrike." As far as I know, MTF Nu-7 is the crew you'd call in to run such as operation, given there talents for making something that exist not exist any more. Or exist in thousands of smaller pieces scattered over a large area. As such, I am recommending the following edits:

Changing this:

Addendum 823-01: Re: Destruction of Site - Per O5-level order, request for immediate destruction of site by air strike is denied due to proximity to civilian population, lack of plausible cover story scenario, and unknown nature of artifact in question.

To this:

Addendum 823-01: Re: Destruction of Site - Per O5-level order, request for immediate destruction of site by air strike, to be lead by MTF Nu-7 ("Hammer Down"), is denied due to proximity to civilian population, lack of plausible cover story scenario, and unknown nature of artifact in question.

item.content:encoded:
It just doesn't do that for me. I have a nagging feeling that there could be so much more to this skip… and it wasn't.

Amusements parks themselves have some underlying creepiness and I've read a few nice creepy pastas about them. So seeing an amusement park SCP I got all excited… and the excitement was gone after about two minutes required to read through this.

I'm new here, so I may not be the person qualified to state what the Foundation is and what it isn't. But I got an impression that among those secure, contain, protect goals there is also a huge stress for examining, learning and generally understanding (or at least trying to understand). And here we have what? One MTF sent? No one thought to throw a few D-class guys there, like they did for almost every other areal scp (that I've read so far)? No special forces, Samsara or whatever else they have in stock? No robots, drones for god's sake? Since one drone was able to get some photos from above, maybe it could examine further? And there were "several violent events". Not a constant flow of violence - what if it's harmful only on certain days or hours? Well, we don't know because, according to the skip, no one ever checked it.

I'm sorry but it just reads as if someone had an awesome idea but got bored halfway through it and rushed to the ending to be over it already.

Is it the location specifically, is it an object that emits "violent bad luck vibes" throughout the area, is it an entity that likes to inflict pain and suffering and if so, what triggered it to start attacking on Bloody Sunday and henceforth if we are to believe that these events came out of nowhere? It all makes for a very chilling thing to ponder and it plays very nicely into the "Gruesome dark twist on a (normally) happy, fun-filled experience".

item.content:encoded:
Meh, I'm on the fence with this one, but in a more drastic sense than usual. There are parts I really like about this and parts I really dislike.

"Tunnel of Love" and "Thriller Chiller" are marked high points with creepy factors played up very well. The idea of being on a roller coaster and watching as row after row the people in front of you get decapitated is terrifying.

Down points are the vague mentions to story fragments such as, "found in the possession of Subject 79." Who/what is subject 79? Were they one of the 7 recovered alive? On of the 231 dead? Something else? No other subjects are mentioned and it feels like I'm just being left out of the loop with just a sampling of what is on "Supplement 823-01-14." Also the MTF "suicides" bother me, but only in a writer sort of way. (I have absolutely no idea how the commander died in a way that was considered suicide. It just seems like suicide was used to one up normal amusement park death.) They don't seem to be inline with the rest of the deaths which were themed around the amusement park and the attendees.

I do think this is one of those scips where you could logically say that they wouldn't risk bombing it, regardless of population nearby, but because we don't know what would happen. Without knowing why this park is doing what it's doing, bombing the place might make things 100 times worse! What if pieces get thrown further and start doing the same anomalous things where they land? What if the physical theme park is what's actually keeping the effects contained?

Anyways, I like parts, but the down points really hurt it in my mind. I am not a big fan of this one. :/ Though I can't say I don't want to read Supplement 823-01-13, "Civilian Deaths Attributed to SCP-823."

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
As much as I hate to at all dislike a Clef SCP…this one just doesn't quite work for me. Yes, it's a brilliant idea, and yes, there's a lot of creep and squick, but it leaves just a little too much to the imagination - enough that it crosses the line between "here's just enough information for your imagination to go wild and give you nightmares" and "here's too little information for your imagination to be able to do much of anything with it". There were a couple of references to cannibalism in the incident reports, but absolutely no indication of who was eating who or what circumstances it might be under. Likewise, the fates met by two of the agents in the mobile task force - dick through the eye and teeth in the lungs - seem to imply some sort of impossible contortion by the victims (given the "suicide" tag), but again, there is absolutely no indication whatsoever of any of the circumstances under which they happened. Same with the guy who ate his ammunition - there's no hint as to what may have caused him to do that. Something as simple as a setting (what "attractions" the agents were in when they met their fates) could easily send the imagination running wild if done right, but in completely lacking even that information, it's just "okay, these freaky things happened to these people somehow, *shrug*".

What bothered me the most was the repeated reference to "the artifact in question"; the use of that phrase led me to believe, for as long as I was reading the article, that there was a specific object or thing that was causing the amusement park to have these anomalies, but it's made clear at the very end that the Foundation has absolutely zero idea what could be causing any of the incidents.

Witholding just enough information to let the reader's imagination do the rest is a tricky thing, and this article simply strays too far to the "not enough" side of the line. No vote. :(
